First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+X-1 \\  & ={X}^{2}+X-I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(A)={A}^{2}+A-I.$

Let's calculate ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & ={A}^{2}+A-I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+3-1 & 0-2+0 \\ 0+4+0 & 1-3-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
